newsitem.title: UK: Japan's emperor, empress to visit Britain.
newsitem.headline: Japan's emperor, empress to visit Britain.

text.p: Japan's Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko will make their first state visit to Britain next year, Queen Elizabeth announced on Wednesday.
It will be the first Japanese state visit to Britain since Emperor Hirohito's in 1971. The date has not yet been set.
The queen made the announcement in her speech to the British parliament outlining the new Labour government's legislative programme for the coming year.
She added that Brazilian President Fernando Cardoso and his wife would visit Britain from December 2 to 5 this year, the first state visit by a Brazilian president for 21 years.
Emperor Akihito visited Britain three times when he was crown prince and attended the queen's coronation in 1953.
The visit is intended to cement relations between London and Tokyo under the new British government, which swept to power with a landslide in the May 1 election.
Japan is Britain's biggest export market outside the European Union and the United States -- British exports to Japan increased by 13 percent in 1996 to 4.3 billion pounds ($7 billion).
Japan is also a big investor in Britain, with more than one thousand of its companies operating here and investments valued at around 20 billion pounds.
Queen Elizabeth also announced that she and her husband Prince Philip would visit India, Pakistan and Canada this year.
